headline: High data-leakage and cascading-error risk: pipecat’s allowlisted egress and shared bus can carry godot_rl_agents outputs into external services without provenance checks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No direct shared channel is documented between godot_rl_agents and pipecat, so prompt injection is not default. However, pipecat supports a shared bus and many text/LLM transports, so if godot_rl_agents output is manually bridged into pipecat, attacker-controlled content could be reinterpreted as instructions. The pathway is indirect and requires unusual configuration.
conditions: IF outputs from godot_rl_agents are copied into pipecat prompts or bus messages
IF pipecat is configured to treat inbound text as instructions without provenance filtering
mitigations: Disable any manual copy-paste bridge between the agents
Add a provenance tag to all bridged messages
Require a human review step before pipecat executes text-derived actions
Use a separate bus topic for untrusted content
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: godot_rl_agents has no network egress, but pipecat has allowlisted egress and touches text, audio, video, images, and conversation state. If the pair shares a workspace or bus, sensitive content entering pipecat can be sent to third-party APIs by default. The blast radius includes multiple work products and conversation state, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF godot_rl_agents outputs are placed into pipecat-managed conversation state
IF pipecat is configured with any external STT/LLM/TTS provider from its documented API surfaces
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable external providers in pipecat for sensitive runs
Route only redacted text into pipecat
Review env.example before launch and remove unused API keys
requires-engineering: enforce egress allowlists per data class

C_capability_conflict.rationale: godot_rl_agents exposes no write or network surfaces in the profile, while pipecat supports shared-bus session state and multiple instances. There is no documented overlapping write target such as a shared filesystem or git state, so direct capability conflict is limited. Uncertainty remains because the orchestrator and any shared mutable resource are not described.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable external resource
IF an orchestrator maps pipecat shared-bus state onto a writable store
mitigations: Assign separate resource namespaces
Avoid shared writable directories
Run one instance per session bus
Check for duplicate writers before enabling both agents
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: pipecat can ingest text and route it through LLM, TTS, and transport services, so if godot_rl_agents output is treated as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or spoken responses. The pair lacks a documented verification step, and pipecat’s broad service surface increases the chance that unverified outputs are propagated.
conditions: IF pipecat consumes godot_rl_agents output as task instructions or facts
IF no verification or human approval step is inserted before downstream actions
mitigations: Insert a validation step before pipecat consumes upstream output
Limit pipecat to read-only rendering for untrusted inputs
Require human approval for any action-taking branch
Log source attribution on every transferred message
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking or schema validation

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for godot_rl_agents, and pipecat’s profile only shows broad data classes and external service integrations. Because the pairwise compliance pathway is not directly evidenced, the main concern is that pipecat may route text or audio to third-party providers under policies not shown here. That is a limited, documentation-gap risk.
conditions: IF regulated data is sent through pipecat to an external provider
IF the operator relies on undocumented retention or residency settings
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared runs
Review provider-specific terms before enabling them
Disable analytics/metrics for sensitive sessions
Keep a local-only configuration for compliance-sensitive workloads
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls per provider
